item.title: Gary Trent Jr. investigation gets quick response from Taylor Jenkins
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Gary Trent Jr. investigation gets quick response from Taylor Jenkins appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NBA’s investigation into Kawhi Leonard and the LA Clippers over cap circumvention was not the only one of that nature that was ongoing. The league had also launched an investigation into the Milwaukee Bucks regarding Gary Trent Jr.‘s new contract in free agency, the results of which have not yet been made public as it’s still an active investigation. In the meantime, Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins was asked about the ongoing investigation into Gary Trent Jr.‘s contract prior to the team’s game against the Los Angeles Lakers, and he acknowledged that his hands were essentially tied as far as commenting on the matter , as per Cameron Ezeir of CBS 58. “I can’t comment on that,” Jenkins responded. “My focus is on day-to-day trying to help this team build winning habits and build our culture. So everything that I’ve been talking about in press conferences, that’s what I’m leaning into with this group. Our focus is right now, how we get better, learn from what happened last night against the Knicks, all the things we’ve been working on the last couple months and try to play our best basketball tonight against the Lakers.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The nine-year veteran guard has been used sparingly by the Bucks this season . He missed four games due to an illness, but hasn’t seen the floor much in the seven games that he has been available to this point. Trent has appeared in only three games at a little over six minutes per game. He’s averaging 3.7 points with splits of 44.4 percent shooting from the field, 42.9 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 61.1 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Related: Bucks rumors: Brian Windhorst warns of guilty verdict, stripped draft picks, suspensions in $64 million Gary Trent Jr. case Related: Bucks’ Taylor Jenkins opens up about building consistency after 7th-straight loss

item.title: ‘They All Viewed It as a Sign’ — Tony Romo’s Appearance on ESPN After CBS Exit Fuels Intrigue Over His Next Career Move
item.description: ‘They All Viewed It as a Sign’ — Tony Romo’s Appearance on ESPN After CBS Exit Fuels Intrigue Over His Next Career Move Tony Romo’s return to television had an audience beyond the fans watching Monday Night Football. People who work with on-air talent were watching, too, and they saw a broadcaster keeping himself in the game. According to Puck’s John Ourand, Romo’s appearance with Pat McAfee offered a clue about his ambitions after leaving CBS. The destination remains uncertain, but several industry observers came away believing he wants another chapter on television. Tony Romo’s McAfee Cameo Catches the Industry’s Attention Romo joined McAfee’s ESPN2 “Field Pass” alternate broadcast during the Buffalo Bills’ 23-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 9. A guest spot was enough to get sports-business executives discussing where he might land next. “Several sports business types who deal with on-air talent were intrigued by Romo’s decision to use McAfee’s alt-cast to make his first post-CBS public appearance,” Ourand wrote . “They all viewed it as a sign that Romo intends to maintain a career in television, either in the booth or in a studio.” That leaves quite a bit of room for his next move. Calling games would put him back in familiar territory. A studio role would offer a different setting for the same football knowledge, with more opportunities to debate and react alongside other personalities. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Ourand’s report described McAfee’s show as a friendly place for Romo to return to analyzing football. One executive summed up the benefit. “This was a safe way to remind people that he’s still out there,” the executive told Ourand. The distinction is useful. These were industry observers interpreting a television appearance, with no new job announcement attached. Still, Romo gave the people who evaluate broadcasters a fresh example of him at work. There is a practical advantage to that. A résumé can list years of major assignments, but an appearance during a live game shows how someone sounds now. McAfee’s format allowed Romo to rejoin the conversation without taking over the entire broadcast. A Television Return Still Needs the Right Opening The speculation moved quickly enough that one sports-business executive predicted to Ourand that Romo could turn up on Netflix’s Christmas Day NFL coverage. Ourand’s reporting tempered that possibility. He indicated that a Netflix assignment was unlikely this season , leaving the holiday prediction well short of a confirmed opportunity. That is the complication behind the interest. Getting executives to talk about a return does not establish that an appropriate opening exists or that a network and Romo have agreed on what his role should be. People who work with on-air talent were watching, too, and they saw a broadcaster keeping himself in the game. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Ourand’s report described McAfee’s show as a friendly place for Romo to return to analyzing football. One executive summed up the benefit. “This was a safe way to remind people that he’s still out there,” the executive told Ourand. The distinction is useful. These were industry observers interpreting a television appearance, with no new job announcement attached. Still, Romo gave the people who evaluate broadcasters a fresh example of him at work. There is a practical advantage to that. A résumé can list years of major assignments, but an appearance during a live game shows how someone sounds now. McAfee’s format allowed Romo to rejoin the conversation without taking over the entire broadcast. A Television Return Still Needs the Right Opening The speculation moved quickly enough that one sports-business executive predicted to Ourand that Romo could turn up on Netflix’s Christmas Day NFL coverage. Ourand’s reporting tempered that possibility. He indicated that a Netflix assignment was unlikely this season , leaving the holiday prediction well short of a confirmed opportunity. That is the complication behind the interest. Getting executives to talk about a return does not establish that an appropriate opening exists or that a network and Romo have agreed on what his role should be. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Romo and CBS mutually parted ways on Oct. 2, ending a partnership that began in 2017. His departure followed a July arrest for operating while intoxicated and a September no-contest plea. In his statement when the split was announced, Romo said he would take time to focus on his health and family before pursuing another opportunity. CBS retained J.J. Watt alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on its lead NFL broadcast team. Monday’s cameo brought Romo back into a familiar environment while allowing viewers to imagine him in a different one. The executives Ourand spoke with considered both the booth and the studio as possible directions, keeping the discussion broader than a single vacancy. Romo’s next employer, assignment, and timetable remain unsettled in that report. But the appearance accomplished something tangible. People who help shape television careers were discussing his future again, and this time they had a fresh football segment to discuss along with it. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Ravens find a new kicker after losing Jake Moody
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Ravens find a new kicker after losing Jake Moody appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It did not take long for the Baltimore Ravens to find a replacement for kicker Jake Moody after he was signed by the Atlanta Falcons to their 53-man roster. Moody was with the Ravens’ practice squad before getting poached by the Falcons. With an open spot, Baltimore eyed a veteran journeyman to fill it, as reported by NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo. “The Ravens are signing former (Miami) Dolphins kicker Riley Patterson following a workout today, source says. Patterson will kick for Baltimore this Monday against the (Los Angeles) Chargers,” wrote Garafolo on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In 22 games for the Dolphins, Patterson converted 34-of-38 field goals for 141 points. The Ravens will be his seventh team in six seasons after also playing for the Detroit Lions, the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Cleveland Browns, the New York Jets, and the Atlanta Falcons. He had two stints with the Lions and the Browns. He was also a practice player for the Minnesota Vikings, the New England Patriots, and the Washington Commanders. Patterson went undrafted in 2021 after a four-year career at Memphis. The Ravens’ signing of Patterson earned mixed reactions on X. “Working out a group of kickers and picking one is so Ravens,” said @SackGambles. “Should have kept Justin Tugger!” wrote @iHardMan302. “The crazy part about it is, every team he’s been on, he’s been solid,” added @TruVisionsz. “Now, let’s hope Baltimore doesn’t leave the game in the kicker’s hands. Please get it together!” pleaded @Charlie_A85. “The way that team is going, they should let me try out. I’m probably just as good,” commented @BKat99. The Ravens will try to end their four-game skid against the Chargers. Related: Ravens’ biggest mistake at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline after adding another center Related: Ravens beat trade deadline buzzer by acquiring Falcons starter in puzzling move

item.title: Defense, a shot-stopper helped Wyoming advance to state final
item.description: SUNBURY, Ohio – Teddy Peterson rejoined the Wyoming High School soccer program this season after focusing on football for the past two years. The Wyoming junior goalkeeper, who has a lot of experience in net in club ball, made the biggest save of his career. He saved the final penalty kick by Bay Village Bay, giving the Cowboys a 6-5 win in the shootout after a 0-0 draw Nov. 11 in the Ohio High School Athletic Association Division IV boys soccer semifinals at Big Walnut High School. Wyoming (16-4-3) plays Worthington Christian in the state final 1 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, the home of the Columbus Crew. Wyoming was 2021 state champions and also made the semis in 2022. Bay finishes 17-2-5. It was a rematch of last year’s state semifinals, when Bay scored late in overtime to win it. “Last year we were at this field,” head coach Ryan Derge said. “They gave us a great fight. We gave them a great fight. We were two minutes away from going to PKs. This is very sweet for all of us, being able to come back and rectify in our minds what we lost." The teams played 110 minutes of scoreless soccer as both teams played intense defense. Wyoming’s best chances came from a couple of headers, which the Bay keeper saved from close range. Bay had a couple of shots from the side clip the crossbar and bounce away, a few inches from being a goal. “Both defenses were good tonight,” Derge said. “You feel it could be (0-0). I think both teams were just so well coached.” Brayden Strong, the senior anchor of the defense, was proud of his whole team. “We were just playing really good as a whole,” he said. “Our midfield was helping out. It was just an outstanding game by everyone today. And it showed at the end when we all got to celebrate with our amazing fans that came out. Just shows how strong our community is, it’s just an amazing feeling.” It went down to penalty kicks. The teams were tied 4-4 after five and then it became one for each team until there was a winner. Both teams made their sixth kick. Junior Liam Hagerman started the seventh round with a successful kick, then Peterson made the save the Cowboys needed. “He got two on his hands and he was able to get the third,” Derge said. “He's quite a shot-stopper. He was a football player. But at Wyoming, we try to make sure that there's a home for every player anywhere they want to meet. And he comes over and coach Jamie is best in the business in terms of developing goalkeepers. So he really works well with Teddy. He's a sponge, and he's probably the most improved from day one to now and it shows.” Said Peterson: “For the first two years of my high school career, I played football and I punted and played receiver. But after a while, I just felt like soccer was more my destiny. I wanted to play both still. But after my sophomore year, I actually felt soccer was my thing.” Wyoming was 6-of-7 in penalty kicks, made by Miles Steininger, Brayden Strong, Tristian Pitman, Ethan Harrison, Cayden Walte

But after my sophomore year, I actually felt soccer was my thing.” Wyoming was 6-of-7 in penalty kicks, made by Miles Steininger, Brayden Strong, Tristian Pitman, Ethan Harrison, Cayden Walters and Hagerman. Steininger wanted to go first and set the tone. “You dream of games like these,” Steininger said. “You love games like these. We were all excited to come here so it's an honor to play in these games.” Players of the game Dawson Feldman, Wyoming : The junior had four great corner kicks in the first half and one in the second half, and one in overtime, which gave the Cowboys a chance to score. Nolan Franco, Wyoming : The senior had two great shot attempts in the first half. One glanced off the top of the crossbar and rolled away. Teddy Peterson, Wyoming : He posted the shutout in goal and made a save to win the PK shootout. Wyoming’s defense : The back line, led by seniors Strong, William Haid and Ethan Nordstrom among others, shut out the Rockets. The Enquirer will update this story with photos from the game. item.title: ‘If LeBron (James) Actually Cared About His New Team…’ — Dave Portnoy Rips 76ers Star for ‘Picking Sides’ Amid Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum Rift
item.description: 'If LeBron (James) Actually Cared About His New Team…' — Dave Portnoy Rips 76ers Star for 'Picking Sides' Amid Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum Rift Barstool Sports’ Dave Portnoy took aim at LeBron James for embracing Jayson Tatum before Tuesday’s highly anticipated showdown between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers, moments after Jaylen Brown appeared to ignore his former teammate. The viral pregame snub came ahead of the Eastern Conference heavyweights’ first regular-season meeting since Brown’s stunning blockbuster trade to Philadelphia over the offseason. After Boston cruised to a 123-101 win, Portnoy used the interaction to take shots at James’ 76ers and compare the two franchises. Dave Portnoy Takes Issue With LeBron James Embracing Jayson Tatum, Questions 76ers Star’s Allegiance Days before the game, Brown said he had “nothing to talk about” with Tatum. The two spent nine seasons together in Boston and helped the Celtics capture the 2024 NBA championship before the franchise abruptly shipped Brown to Philadelphia for Paul George and draft capital. Brown showed no visible reaction when Tatum walked over moments before tipoff, tapped him on the shoulder, and patted his chest. The pair also kept to opposite ends of the floor throughout warmups. READ MORE: ‘I Wasn’t Paying Attention’ — 76ers Star Jaylen Brown Offers Blunt Justification For Viral Jayson Tatum Snub Tatum then turned to James, who stood right beside Brown, and the two shook hands and traded a big hug, immediately raising eyebrows. Portnoy was among those who saw more than a pregame greeting. “I don’t want to read into this too much, but doesn’t this sum up the Celtics vs. Sixers franchises in a nutshell? The Celtics is about class and being a brotherhood. Jaylen ignores Tatum, and then LeBron basically does the Macarena with JT,” Portnoy tweeted . Portnoy saved his sharpest words for the four-time MVP: “If LeBron actually cared about his new team and teammates, wouldn’t he have toned down his love for Tatum? Bron basically picked sides, and he picked Tatum and the Celtics.” Asked afterward about the pregame interaction, Brown steered the conversation back to his own team and appeared unbothered by James showing love to his ex-co-star. “I’m just focused on coming out and doing what’s best for my team. Everything else was just — to be honest, I wasn’t paying attention. But credit to Jayson. He played well tonight,” Brown said. Tatum likewise played down the exchange, explaining, “No headlines about anything like that. I was just getting ready for the game.” Portnoy went on to connect the lopsided nature of the contest to the sides’ pregame demeanor: “And then the Celtics thoroughly kicked their [expletive] up and down the court all night. One team played together as one heartbeat, and the other was 5 players, 5 balls, 5 egos.” Philadelphia’s only lead came at 5-4 in the first quarter, and after the 76ers tied the game at 79-79 late in the third, Boston pulled away. The Celtics led by as many as 29 points as George scored 14 of his game-high 36 points in the fourth quarter. READ MORE: ‘Downright Terrible,’ ‘Celtics Won the Trade’ – Dave Portnoy, NBA World Rip Jaylen Brown’s No-Show in Highly Anticipated Revenge Game vs. Jayson Tatum On the flip side, Brown’s evening unraveled fast, with 2 fouls in the first quarter and a 4th early in the third. I was locked in. I was focused, I was ready to go,” Brown said. “Foul trouble kind of took me out of my rhythm a little bit. I had to sit for a while, and we didn’t execute as well as they did.” The loss dropped the 76ers to 9-3 and second in the East, half a game behind the Celtics (9-2), with their next matchup scheduled for Jan. 21 in Boston. item.title: Trevor Megill Misses Out on NL Reliever of the Year Award 2026
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill (29) celebrates after winning Game 5 and World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Oct 28, 2026. Mark Hoffman / Milwaukee Journal Sentinel / USA TODA… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Milwaukee Brewers are still basking in the glow of their first World Series title , but their star in the bullpen, Trevor Megill, has missed out on National League Reliever of the Year. The reliever was 30/33 in save opportunities in the regular season while posting a 0.89 WHIP, 2.63 ERA, and striking out 69 in 61 2/3 IP. The Brewers chose to rely heavily on their bullpen during their NLCS win and during the World Series, and Megill was central to that strategy. He matched his WHIP from the regular season in eight appearances while saving five games. Trevor Megill Loses NL Reliever of the Year Megill didn’t have a clear path to the majors for the first several years of his career, bouncing between the San Diego Padres, Chicago Cubs and Minnesota Twins. He was eventually traded to the Brewers in 2023 for a player to be named later, in this case Taylor Floyd , who never reached Major League Baseball. It was in Milwaukee that Megill began to thrive, becoming their full-time closer during the 2024 season en route to being named to the 2025 All-Star team, his first accolade. Oct 28, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill (29) throws a pitch against the Tampa Bay Rays during the ninth inning in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images In fact, Megill has improved every year since being acquired. The California native made 31 appearances in 2023 with a 3.63 ERA, while he pitched in 48 games as the full-time closer in 2024, putting up an ERA of 2.72. It could be said that Megill is aging like a fine wine, with 2026, his age 32 season, being his best to date. Brewers Dominate Trevor Hoffman Award The NL Reliever of the Year award is named in honor of Trevor Hoffman, and since its inception in 2014, no team has won it more times (five) than the Brewers. Josh Hader won it three times (2018, 2019, 2021), while Devin Williams is a two-time winner (2020, 2023). The New York Mets are the next leading team in winning the award, having done so twice thanks to Edwin Diaz (2022, 2025). However, Megill was unable to compete with runaway winner Mason Miller, who won 100% of the first-place votes in the 2026 edition of the award. The Brewers closer finished a distant third, behind both Miller and Jhoan Duran, but ahead of new free agents Adrian Morejon and Raisel Iglesias . The crown jewel, of c

item.title: ‘Absolute Insanity That It Took This Long,’ ‘He Actually Had To Call the NFL Out’ — Bengals QB Joe Burrow’s SNF Milestone Leaves Fans Stunned
item.description: ‘Absolute Insanity That It Took This Long,’ ‘He Actually Had To Call the NFL Out’ — Bengals QB Joe Burrow’s SNF Milestone Leaves Fans Stunned Joe Burrow has played enough big games that a Sunday night date with the Pittsburgh Steelers should barely register as a career first. Somehow, this one does. The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback is set to play in his first home, divisional primetime game. The discovery left Cincinnati fans checking the calendar and wondering how the NFL managed to make them wait this long. Bengals Fans Stunned by Joe Burrow’s Long-Awaited Primetime First Cincinnati hosts Pittsburgh at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 15, giving Burrow a chance to check off a surprisingly stubborn box in his seventh NFL season. Both teams enter the matchup at 6-2, with first place in the AFC North up for grabs. The unusual first has left fans wondering how this hadn’t happened sooner. “Absolute insanity that it took this long,” one fan wrote . Another fan had considerably less patience for the league. “Pathetic,” they wrote , “Seven years, and the guy finally gets some respect.” “Wait… excuse me?” a third fan asked . Burrow has been one of the league’s most recognizable quarterbacks for years, making the lack of a primetime home game against a division rival all the more unusual. “He actually had to call the NFL out to get it too,” one fan added . Burrow publicly questioned the scheduling in May 2025 after the Bengals were scheduled for a fourth consecutive season with a primetime road game against Baltimore. His request was simple. “Maybe we can get one of those in Cincinnati? Please,” Burrow said. NFL scheduling executive Mike North acknowledged that Burrow’s complaint was fair . That history helps explain why fans were quick to connect his past comments to Sunday’s matchup. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor An X account named “NFL Schedule Enthusiast” laid out Burrow’s history of primetime divisional games in a post. They listed seven matchups, all on the road: a 2020 Thursday night game at Cleveland, two games at Baltimore and Cleveland in 2022, a Thursday night game at Baltimore in 2023, another at Baltimore in 2024, a Saturday game at Pittsburgh that season, and a Thanksgiving matchup at Baltimore in 2025. “That’s insane… INSANE,” another fan remarked . BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Burrow did start Cincinnati’s 24-17 Wild-Card win over Baltimore at home on a Sunday night in January 2023. However, this week’s milestone applies specifically to the regular season. The Bengals also hosted Pittsburgh in primetime in 2020 and 2025, but Burrow missed both games due to injuries. Ryan Finley and Joe Flacco started those matchups, respectively. A scheduled Thursday night home game against Cleveland in December 2024 was also moved to Sunday afternoon. So the lack of a regular-season primetime home game against a division rival comes down to both scheduling and missed opportunities. Cincinnati ha

item.title: Walker Kessler joins elite club in quick fashion
item.description: The Lakers’ Walker Kessler grabbed his 2,000th rebound against the Bucks on Wednesday, becoming the 11th-fastest player in NBA history to reach 2,000-plus points, 2,000-plus rebounds and 500-plus blocks. Kessler is the third-fastest active player to reach that line, trailing only Victor Wembanyama and Anthony Davis. Los Angeles Lakers’ Walker Kessler dunks during an NBA basketball game against the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, in Milwaukee. AP Photo/Aaron Gash Kessler is averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 rebounds and 2.3 blocks for the Lakers, who entered Wednesday’s game with the league’s best record (10-2). Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) shoots against Atlanta Hawks forward Onyeka Okongwu (17) in an NBA basketball game, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in Atlanta. AP Photo/Mike Stewart The Lakers acquired Kessler in July in a sign-and-trade from the Jazz for two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps on top of a four-year, $130 million deal. The 25-year-old Kessler only played five games last season after suffering a torn labrum in his left shoulder that required surgery. Kessler has made an immediate impact for the Lakers, who have won six games in a row . He entered Wednesday’s game leading the NBA in contested shots (140) and has been their defensive anchor , finishing with a double-double in six of his last seven contests. This story will be updated.

item.title: 7 free agents Chiefs should consider signing after NFL trade deadline
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs acquired star wide receiver Josh Downs in a last-minute deal with the Indianapolis Colts at the 2026 NFL trade deadline, but general manager Brett Veach's work is far from over. While the Chiefs can no longer trade for new players, the pool of veteran talent still available in free agency is astonishing. From All-Pro wide receivers to a Pro Bowl offensive lineman and a former NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year, Kansas City's front office doesn't lack options if it wants to land one more big-name talent to shore up the Chiefs' depth chart for the second half of the 2026 regular season. Here are seven free agents Kansas City should take a look at in the coming days and weeks: WR Tyreek Hill Perhaps the most obvious choice, a reunion with Hill would be totally transformative for the Chiefs' offense — assuming the five-time All-Pro wideout is fully healthy and ready to play. OT Taylor Decker This 2024 Pro Bowler could help bring stability to the edges of Kansas City's offensive line and give Decker an opportunity to chase a ring while protecting Patrick Mahomes. DB Marshon Lattimore Kansas City is rumored to have pursued cornerbacks at the trade deadline, but the addition of Lattimore — the 2017 NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year — would be a shot in the arm for Steve Spagnuolo's defense. WR Curtis Samuel Though he may have lost a step, Samuel could help Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes as a versatile runner-receiver with legitimate big-play ability. OL Jonah Williams Williams has plenty of experience blocking for an elite quarterback in Joe Burrow, but the Chiefs would have to do their due diligence on the shoulder injury that prematurely ended his 2025 campaign with the Arizona Cardinals . DB Jimmie Ward Though he hasn't played since 2024, Ward's veteran savvy could be just what Kansas City's secondary needs in the back half of the regular season. DL Joey Bosa A longtime Chiefs nemesis after a career spent with the Los Angeles Chargers and Buffalo Bills , the addition of Bosa would give Kansas City a tested pass-rusher with plenty of motivation to win a championship in what would be his eleventh NFL season. This article originally appeared on Chiefs Wire: 7 free agents Chiefs should consider signing after NFL trade deadline

item.title: NC State Moves To Top Tier Of ACC With Hiring Of Philip Rivers
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Bringing back NC State icon, NFL star Philip Rivers is a home-run hire for the football program and school. Philip Rivers is the only name that could help bring NC State football back into contention in the ACC. While the Wolfpack becoming an overnight contender for the College Football Playoff might be too much to ask, competing in the conference is not. Related: Miami With Best Path To College Football Playoff Title Game Rivers brings name value, and that is something you cannot ignore anymore. Not when it comes to money in college athletics and NIL swirling over the heads of everyone involved. Philip Rivers Set To Become The Next Head Football Coach At NC State According to multiple reports, a contract making Rivers the head football coach at NC State will be finalized on Friday. He asked to conclude his sixth season as head football coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama. Of course, we all remember when he briefly returned to the NFL after coaching high school athletes. Related: Iowa Deserves Position In Latest College Football Playoff Ranking Now, the 44-year-old is set to make the ultimate jump from the high school ranks to big-time college football. Success Followed Philip Rivers From The NFL To High School Football In Alabama Immediately, Rivers turned St. Michael Catholic into a contender in Alabama high school football. The Cardinals reached the state semifinals in both 2024 and again in 2025 under his guidance. Heading into this season, Rivers held a record of 44-16 overall, including a 25-9 mark while competing in Class 4A. Both years that St. Michael Catholic reached the final four, they lost to Jackson. This season, the Cardinals slipped to 6-5 overall, but went 5-2 in regional play, finishing third. They lost starting quarterback Gunner Rivers, Philip Rivers’ son, in the season opener. The younger Rivers would return after missing several games before returning in October. Top Talent Will Want To Play For NC State, Philip Rivers You better believe quarterbacks coming up through the high school ranks are going to want to play for Rivers. He knows everybody, has seen everything and has incredible connections to the NFL. High-end quarterback recruits will be flooding NC State under Rivers, and that will also bring top wide receivers, running backs, linemen and more to the program. Heck, he already has one, as Gunner Rivers committed earlier this year after a prep career that saw him throw for over 10,000 yards and 100 touchdowns. Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: Three Takeaways From the Flames' 3-1 Loss to the Rangers
item.description: The Calgary Flames came up short Wednesday night, falling 3-1 to the New York Rangers at the Scotiabank Saddledome. After a scoreless opening period, the Rangers needed just 59 seconds in the second to get on the board. Mika Zibanejad carried the puck into the Calgary zone, drove wide and fired a shot from a sharp angle that beat Cooley to give New York a 1-0 lead. Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Zibanejad struck again at 10:52, this time on the power play. After the Rangers moved the puck around the Calgary zone, Pavel Dorofeyev found Zibanejad at the top of the circle for a one-timer. The shot beat Cooley through the body and glove to make it 2-0. The Flames found an answer on the power play in the third period. At 7:41, Yegor Sharangovich sent the puck down low to Ryan Strome, who quickly spotted Adam Klapka in front of the net. Klapka jammed the puck past Joonas Korpisalo for his fourth goal of the season, cutting the deficit to 2-1. Calgary couldn’t find the equalizer, and Ty Kartye sealed the Rangers’ victory with an empty-net goal. Three Takeaways 1. Cooley’s strong home run comes to an end Cooley entered Wednesday’s game with an impressive 5-0-0 record in his previous five home starts, posting a 1.78 goals-against average and a .946 save percentage over that stretch. The Rangers handed him his first loss during that run, scoring twice in the second period to take control of the game. 2. Parekh continues to show his offensive potential Zayne Parekh provided one of Calgary’s more exciting moments in the opening period. The young defenceman carried the puck through the Rangers’ defence on an impressive individual rush, dangling his way toward the net before attempting to wrap around. Korpisalo got his blocker on the attempt to keep the game scoreless, but it was another glimpse of Parekh’s offensive creativity and ability to generate chances on his own. 3. Sharangovich continues to produce Sharangovich picked up an assist on Klapka’s third-period goal, extending a productive stretch for the Flames forward. He now has four points (one goal, three assists) over his last four games, providing some consistent offensive production for Calgary.

item.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Running Back Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Cam Skattebo vs. Rachaad White
item.description: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Week 10 of fantasy football has arrived, and with it come the usual calls of who to start and who to sit. Thursday Night Football kicks us off with the Washington Commanders against the New York Giants. Cam Skattebo is healthy again for the Giants, while Rachaad White had double-digit fantasy football performances in Weeks 6 and 8. Which running back should fantasy managers start in this class TNF matchup? RB Cam Skattebo, New York Giants In his second season in the NFL, Skattebo is averaging 10.1 fantasy points per week, putting him around RB28 status. With a matchup against the Commanders, who have allowed 694 rushing yards this season, and recent injuries to key defensive players, Skattebo looks favorable in Week 10. The Commanders held Skattebo in check in Week 5, allowing the Giants' running back only 59 yards on 13 carries. But with injuries to Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, the Commanders rush defense has slipped in recent weeks. The Commanders have allowed six rushing touchdowns this season, and Skattebo will be looking to add to his tally of two touchdowns on the season. Skattebo will be the main RB for the Giants, with Devin Singletary acting as his backup. RB Rachaad White, Washington Commanders Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White (1) rushes during the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect White is averaging 10.0 fantasy points this season, but he has put up impressive fantasy point totals in Weeks 2, 6, and 8. Against the Giants, White only managed 3.0 fantasy points, but he was coming off of a shoulder injury that kept him out of Week 4. item.content:encoded: 17/7/10 for Elliot Cadeau, kind of bad to not contain the obvious threat | Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images Shouts to Loyal Reader MUAlways, who had a terrific summary of the 40 minutes of nightmare in Ann Arbor that we watched on Wednesday night, as YOUR Marquette Golden Eagles men’s basketball team took an 84-70 loss to #20 Michigan: Lemme double check the stat sheet just for confirmation…. yep, that is all 100% accurate, and whatever else was going on — and we’ll talk about some of it here — that’s definitely the short version of what went wrong for Marquette here. You’re not going to win a lot of ball games when your All-American hopeful point guard shoots 0-for-11 and commits four turnovers to end up as a -27 in just 18 minutes before the head coach nails him to the bench with 10:46 to play. You’re not going to win a lot of ball games when your scoring tilted big man goes 2-for-13, including misses on all three of his triples. You’re not going to win a lot of ball games when your $4 million transfer big man gets foul limited to 22 minutes, attempts just three shots all game, and finishes with more fouls than rebounds and the same number of turnovers as rebounds. And yet, it is so much worse than that simplistic explanation. With 8:56 left in the first half, Colin Porter hit a legally assisted three-pointer to put Marquette up 22-15 on the Wolverines. That was an 11-2 run by the Golden Eagles at the time. Michigan answered with 13 straight and a 20-5 run to the end of the first half that left the home team up 35-27 at the break. See? Worse! JP Estrella opened up the second half with a three for Michigan, and then the Wolverines answered a Damarius Owens triple with two more of their own, BOOM: 14 point margin. The problem there, of course, is that Marquette lacked a counterpunch coming out of the locker room, and now they were in massive amounts of trouble. This led to what I believe was at the Under 12 minutes timeout in the second half. I know it was before Sananda Fru hit a three for his first (and ultimately only ) bucket of the game, and that was at 9:47. During the timeout, FS1 went into the Marquette huddle and we got to see head coach Shaka Smart point out to his team that this, all of this, building a lead, looking calm and confident, and then melting down to the tune of a 42-14 run, is how they were responding to their first road game of the season, their first game against a ranked team of the season, their first game against a high major opponent of the season. Smart did it in a very Made For TV way, extremely polite, extremely straightforward, extremely direct, everyone knew what he meant, and then he redirected that to note that all of the problems they had created for themselves now presented an opportunity to show what they were made of for the final 10 minutes of the game. In other words: Smart asked his team if they were planning on stinking this bad all season when faced with the slightest bit of adversity, and if not, what were they going to do about it right here and right now? And honestly: That trick nearly worked. 8-0 run to cut the margin to 14. 7-0 run to get it to just nine points with 7:14 left. Wait, is this a ball game now? No, it wasn’t. Michigan pushed it back to 16, 69-53, on a Trey McKinney jumper with 5:18 to go, and that was probably all she wrote there. But that’s not 22, Michigan’s largest lead of the game, or a number bigger than that. We do have to note that Colin Porter nearly dragged the team kicking and screaming into something happening down the stretch. A pair of threes and a layup from the Liberty transfer slashed the game back down to single digits, 64-73, with 2:17 to play. I swear to you, it felt like I raised an eyebrow in curiosity at this development, and then blinked, and when I opened my eyes, Michigan was up 17. I am only slightly exaggerating. It took 51 seconds of game time. The official final margin is 14, but hooooboy, it was almost so much worse after getting it inside of 10 with two and change to play. Honestly, that makes the whole thing even worse, because they needed four points in the final 30 seconds to make the final score look mildly not irresponsible. Marquette is now 2-1 on the season, and more importantly, 0-1 in the six games that matter before Big East play starts . Highlights, such as they are, courtesy of GoMarquette.com and FS1: Up Next: It is very important that Marquette doesn’t stink on Sunday. Next up for the Golden Eagles is another game away from Fiserv Forum, but at least this one is a neutral site game with very few tickets sold. On Sunday, Marquette will be down in Chicago at the United Center for a game against Missouri. Tipoff is set for 1:30pm Central, and Peacock will have the broadcast. The Tigers are 2-1 after beating SIUE by 38 on Monday, with the loss coming in Saint Louis to Saint Louis, 90-84. item.title: ‘Injury-Prone WRs Are What They Do’ — NFL Analyst Makes Feelings Clear on 49ers’ Surprise Keenan Allen Trade
item.description: ‘Injury-Prone WRs Are What They Do’ — NFL Analyst Makes Feelings Clear on 49ers’ Surprise Keenan Allen Trade The San Francisco 49ers have had their fair share of injury problems over the past few seasons, particularly on offense. The 2026 campaign has been especially brutal, with the team running short on healthy wide receivers. Sitting atop the NFC West, the 49ers naturally added some much-needed help at the trade deadline, acquiring veteran Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts. However, the move has already drawn some jokes from fans, and NFL analyst Colin Cowherd also couldn’t resist taking a shot at San Francisco for its habit of bringing in older receivers with injury histories. Colin Cowherd Takes a Shot at 49ers Over Keenan Allen Trade The 49ers had little choice but to address their depleted receiving corps. Mike Evans remains sidelined, while Deebo Samuel returned to limited practice Wednesday after missing three games with a hamstring injury. De’Zhaun Stribling is likely out until December, and Ricky Pearsall is done for the season. With so few reliable options available, San Francisco needed help. The team eventually traded a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Colts for Allen, according to NFL insider Adam Schefter . At 34, Allen is no longer in his prime, and his injury history hasn’t helped his case. That gave Cowherd an opening to take a shot at the 49ers for once again turning to an aging receiver with a history of health issues. “You gotta appreciate the commitment to the bit. That’s sort of what the Niners did. Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch signing another old WR with injury history… I appreciate the 49ers believing in this bit. Injury-prone wide receivers are what they do,” Cowherd said on “The Herd.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Cowherd also brought up Brock Purdy’s numbers, joking how often he’s connected with receivers over 30 years old this season. “Brock Purdy has 17 touchdown passes this year, with 16 to guys over 30, or guys in their thirties. This is what they are,” the analyst continued. Through Week 9, Allen ranks No. 52 with a PFN WR Impact Score of 72.1. He joins Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins among San Francisco’s available receiving options. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The 49ers now have Evans, Allen, Samuel, and Brandin Cooks, which is Cowherd’s point. These are some of the oldest receivers in the NFL, but San Francisco is hoping they can still produce at a high level. Cooks hasn’t been called upon as much, but Evans, Allen, and Samuel are key contributors for the team. Allen certainly addresses a need for the Niners, and, at worst, he is a solid veteran depth piece. The 49ers are well-positioned to win the NFC West if they stay healthy, keep playing well, and take care of business in their divisional matchups. After 14 years in the league, he may finally have a chance to get his hands on the Lombardi Trophy. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Son Heung-min says divisions at heart of South Korea team resolved
item.description: Son Heung-min has been called up by South Korea for friendlies next month against Saudi Arabia and Qatar (Philip FONG) Son Heung-min and four other South Korean players said Thursday they had put their differences aside after reports of bitter internal divisions at the heart of the national team. South Korean football has been mired in controversy since their hugely disappointing exit in the group stage of the World Cup, after which unpopular coach Hong Myung-bo quit. In the fallout, reports emerged in local media of a split involving the 34-year-old skipper Son and some of the other players, including Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae. Son and Kim, together with Lee Jae-sung, Hwang In-beom and Hwang Hee-chan, issued a joint statement to fans apologising and saying it was time to move on after they held talks. "First of all we would like to sincerely apologise to the Korean public and football fans for the concern caused by recent reports concerning the national team," the statement said. "At our recent meeting we gathered to share our thoughts on the national team openly and honestly. "By listening directly to one another and discussing matters we had not had sufficient opportunities to address, we were able to gain a better understanding of each other's positions." During their talks they said they looked at what went wrong at the World Cup, admitting they were still hurting from the experience. "Our discussions began with the question of what needs to change to ensure that we do not repeat the same mistakes," they said in the statement. They added: "We now intend to put unnecessary controversy behind us and focus on building a stronger national team together." Spanish coach Robert Moreno took over from Hong on an interim basis, with his contract reportedly set to expire this month. South Korea play Saudi Arabia in Qatar on Friday before another friendly, against Qatar, four days later. The matches were originally designed as build-up to the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia but the tournament was last week postponed to December next year. bur-pst/dh

item.title: ‘That’s Not Really Who He Is’ — NFL Analyst Pushes Chiefs To Rethink Xavier Worthy’s Role Following Josh Downs Trade
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Xavier Worthy and wide receiver Josh Downs. The Kansas City Chiefs have spent much of the season trying to find the right balance in their passing attack. Injuries and changes across the receiving corps have forced players into roles that do not always suit their strengths. The arrival of Josh Downs gives Patrick Mahomes another option, but it could also change how Kansas City uses one of its fastest playmakers. ESPN analyst Jordan Rodgers believes that adjustment could be exactly what Xavier Worthy needs. Jordan Rodgers Explains How Josh Downs Trade Could Help Xavier Worthy Rodgers believes the Chiefs should stop asking Worthy to handle so many routes over the middle and return him to the responsibilities that made him dangerous. Speaking on ESPN’s “Get Up,” the former undrafted NFL quarterback said Downs’ route-running ability could take pressure off Worthy and allow Kansas City’s receivers to operate in more suitable roles. “I think what it does, though, is it allows them to use Worthy as the guy that he is, the gadget guy and the take-the-top-off guy, too. Too much right now, they’re using him over the middle of the field to try to run routes and get open. That’s not really who he is,” Rodgers said. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator He pointed to Downs’ ability to create separation on intermediate routes as a major reason for the change. Rodgers added, “Josh Downs… is fourth in the NFL in getting open 10-plus, 20-plus, and 10 to 20 yards. So, he creates separation. I think it kind of allows everybody else to fall into their natural roles as well.” Downs gives Kansas City a receiver who can work through the middle and win against man coverage. He is ranked 37th on PFN’s WR Impact Metric and has caught 33 passes for 354 yards and a touchdown this season with Indianapolis. His separation skills could give Mahomes a reliable option on shorter and intermediate throws. That would allow Worthy to return to a more specialized role on the perimeter. Kansas City could use his 4.21-second speed on deep routes while creating touches through motion, jet sweeps, and quick screens. With Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve after dislocating his left ankle and tearing ligaments, Worthy remains one of Kansas City’s primary vertical threats. item.title: ‘LeBron (James) on LePoster,’ ‘Zero Gravity’ — Jayson Tatum’s Monster Dunk Over 76ers Star Sends NBA World Into Frenzy
item.description: Jayson Tatum’s dunk over LeBron James brings back 2018 memories and sparks reactions during his first matchup with Jaylen Brown. Jayson Tatum dunked on LeBron James during the Boston Celtics’ 123-101 rout of the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night, bringing back memories of a moment from eight years earlier and sparking plenty of reaction online. The game also carried another storyline for the six-time All-Star, who was facing Jaylen Brown for the first time since his longtime Celtics teammate was traded to Philadelphia. NBA Community Reacts to Jayson Tatum’s LeBron James Poster and Jaylen Brown Moment The dunk came with 6:06 left in the third quarter, one possession after Tatum blocked VJ Edgecombe’s layup and grabbed the rebound. He then worked through a double team before throwing down a one-handed rim-rattling slam over James to push Boston’s lead to 73-67. “It just kind of felt good to finish through contact. It’s been about 19 months since I dunked on somebody. Just to kind of get my legs back, feeling good, it’s a basketball play,” the 28-year-old said after the game . By Wednesday morning, the Celtics had summed up the play in two words: “Zero gravity.” “Pardon My Take” had its own description : “Tatum puts LeBron on LePoster.” The dunk also immediately drew comparisons to Tatum’s rookie season, when he threw one down over the four-time NBA MVP in Game 7 of the 2018 Eastern Conference finals. “Tatum turned back the clock on LeBron,” SportsCenter wrote . Barstool Sports Celtics analyst Dan Greenberg added : “Time is a flat circle.” The attention then shifted to Brown, whose first meeting with his former teammate had already drawn interest before tipoff. After the dunk, Brick Center reacted : “Tatum dunked on LeBron. The camera IMMEDIATELY cut to Jaylen Brown.” NBA/NFL insider Matt Wallace also highlighted their pregame interaction. “Jayson Tatum walked over before tip-off tonight to show love to his old teammate Jaylen Brown. Tapped his arm, tapped his chest, nothing but respect. Brown looked right through him. Wouldn’t even acknowledge him. Just kept spinning the ball like Tatum didn’t exist. Tatum took the high road and let it go,” Wallace noted . The 2024 NBA Finals MVP later said he had not been focused on the exchange. “I’m just focused on coming out and doing what’s best for my team. Everything else was just, to be honest, I wasn’t paying attention. But credit to Jayson. He played well tonight,” Brown said . Brown finished with 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting in 26 minutes, along with 4 turnovers and a game-worst minus-27. Asked about the same pregame moment, Tatum dismissed the idea that there was anything more to it. “Like I said, there are no headlines about anything like that. I was just getting ready for the game, ready for jump ball, go out there, compete, have some fun, and try to get a win,” he said . The Boston forward finished with 21 points on 8-for-17 shooting, 6 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 blocks in 32 minutes. SEE ALSO: ‘It

Jayson Tatum dunked on LeBron James during the Boston Celtics’ 123-101 rout of the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night, bringing back memories of a moment from eight years earlier and sparking plenty of reaction online. NBA Community Reacts to Jayson Tatum’s LeBron James Poster and Jaylen Brown Moment The dunk came with 6:06 left in the third quarter, one possession after Tatum blocked VJ Edgecombe’s layup and grabbed the rebound. He then worked through a double team before throwing down a one-handed rim-rattling slam over James to push Boston’s lead to 73-67. “It just kind of felt good to finish through contact. It’s been about 19 months since I dunked on somebody. Just to kind of get my legs back, feeling good, it’s a basketball play,” the 28-year-old said after the game . By Wednesday morning, the Celtics had summed up the play in two words: “Zero gravity.” “Pardon My Take” had its own description : “Tatum puts LeBron on LePoster.” The dunk also immediately drew comparisons to Tatum’s rookie season, when he threw one down over the four-time NBA MVP in Game 7 of the 2018 Eastern Conference finals. “Tatum turned back the clock on LeBron,” SportsCenter wrote . Barstool Sports Celtics analyst Dan Greenberg added : “Time is a flat circle.” The attention then shifted to Brown, whose first meeting with his former teammate had already drawn interest before tipoff. After the dunk, Brick Center reacted : “Tatum dunked on LeBron. The camera IMMEDIATELY cut to Jaylen Brown.” NBA/NFL insider Matt Wallace also highlighted their pregame interaction. “Jayson Tatum walked over before tip-off tonight to show love to his old teammate Jaylen Brown. Tapped his arm, tapped his chest, nothing but respect. Brown looked right through him. Wouldn’t even acknowledge him. Just kept spinning the ball like Tatum didn’t exist. Tatum took the high road and let it go,” Wallace noted . The 2024 NBA Finals MVP later said he had not been focused on the exchange. “I’m just focused on coming out and doing what’s best for my team. Everything else was just, to be honest, I wasn’t paying attention. But credit to Jayson. He played well tonight,” Brown said . Brown finished with 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting in 26 minutes, along with 4 turnovers and a game-worst minus-27. Asked about the same pregame moment, Tatum dismissed the idea that there was anything more to it. “Like I said, there are no headlines about anything like that. I was just getting ready for the game, ready for jump ball, go out there, compete, have some fun, and try to get a win,” he said . The Boston forward finished with 21 points on 8-for-17 shooting, 6 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 blocks in 32 minutes. SEE ALSO: ‘It Feels Natural’ – NBA Analyst Details Why Paul George Is a ‘Better Fit’ With Jayson Tatum Than Jaylen Brown One fan put it simply : “Jayson Tatum handled his business against the 76ers.” Boston improved to 9-2 with the win, while Paul George led all scorers with 36 points against the team that traded him. Tatum and Brown are scheduled to meet again on Jan. 21, when the 76ers visit TD Garden for the teams’ first regular-season matchup in Boston since the trade. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Giants’ Malik Nabers Calls Out FOX and Greg Olsen for ‘Lie’ About His Demeanor
item.description: The New York Giants earned a 19–11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, but Malik Nabers’ on-field reactions drew attention during the broadcast. His body language became a subject of criticism from FOX analysts Joe Davis and Greg Olsen. The comments prompted the wide receiver to address questions about his approach and relationship with teammates. Giants’ Malik Nabers defends his conduct as a teammate New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers responded to FOX broadcasters Joe Davis and Greg Olsen after they criticized his body language during Sunday’s win over the Philadelphia Eagles. ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky had previously described Nabers as an increasingly dangerous weapon as the Giants expanded his role in the slot. Nabers rejected the criticism, saying it misrepresented who he is as a player and teammate. Jul 24, 2025; East Rutherford, NJ, USA; New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (1) celebrates with offensive tackle James Hudson III (55) during training camp at Quest Diagnostics Training Center. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Nabers finished the game with five catches on eight targets for 43 yards, with a long reception of 22 yards. It was his first game below 100 receiving yards since Week 3, ending a streak of four consecutive 100-yard performances. He also failed to score a touchdown. During the fourth quarter, cameras captured Nabers expressing frustration after failing to connect with J.J. McCarthy on a pass. Davis and Olsen criticized his body language during the broadcast, questioning his reaction to the team’s success. Nabers said: “I feel like that was just a lie, attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate.” He added, “Don’t tell the world who I am if you don’t know who I am.” The criticism also followed Nabers’ lack of visible celebration after Isaiah Likely scored a five-yard touchdown to give the Giants the lead in the fourth quarter. Olsen emphasized that players should support their teammates’ success rather than let their desire to receive the ball affect how they respond to others’ achievements. Nabers later addressed the discussion on social media, asking people to stop criticizing his reactions on the field. He also said that none of his teammates had ever questioned his commitment to the team and suggested that cameras should focus elsewhere if viewers disliked his reactions. Speaking to reporters Tuesday, Nabers explained that his facial expressions and demeanor remain the same regardless of whether he plays well or poorly, or whether the Giants win or lose. He described himself as a competitive player who expects the same level of commitment from those around him. He said his reactions stem from his passion for the game rather than disappointment in others. Giants head coach John Harbaugh also defended Nabers, saying television footage does not provide a complete picture of a player’s mindset. item.title: Frankie Muniz breaks silence after NASCAR crash: 'My Mustang did its job'
item.description: Frankie Muniz is offering an update on his health after the actor and NASCAR driver crashed in Florida during a practice drive. The " Malcolm in the Middle " alum, 40, was released from the hospital Wednesday evening, Nov. 11, after the crash. "I am a little sore, but my Mustang did its job in protecting me," Muniz said in a statement via Ford Racing. "I want to thank everyone at Ford Racing, Daytona International Speedway and the staff here at the hospital. I especially want to thank everyone who has reached out and for all the prayers." More: Frankie Muniz hospitalized after accident at Daytona ahead of Ford exhibition race The Emmy-nominated actor, who competes in the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series, was hospitalized on Nov. 11 after crashing at Daytona International Speedway, Ford and Muniz's Team Reaume announced in an earlier statement, adding that he was "awake and alert." The practice drive came ahead of Ford’s " Proud To Honor Veterans Day Classic ," where he was initially set to drive before the crash. The track was not open to the public at the time, according to Team Reaume. Ford development driver and International Motor Sports Association competitor Jenson Altzman, 24, replaced Muniz during the exhibition race. Muniz said in a statement that he was "disappointed" he couldn't compete in the event at Daytona's road course. Entertainment Tonight shared images from Getty showing heavy damage to Muniz's racecar with the roof removed. The outlet reported that Muniz's "Malcolm in the Middle" co-star Bryan Cranston was expected to watch the race. The crash was not due to a vehicle malfunction, NASCAR driver Brad Keselowski told reporters before the event. "The team here at Ford Racing looked through all the data and didn’t find anything happened to the car (before the crash)," Keselowski said. "I think we’re all pretty comfortable." NASCAR driver Ryan Blaney was also slated to race in the exhibition but withdrew on Nov. 10 after he "accidentally took a fall that required medical attention." Muniz rose as a Hollywood star at a young age with 1997 TV movies "To Dance with Olivia" and "What the Deaf Man Heard" before landing his breakout role on the classic sitcom "Malcolm in the Middle." He's also starred in movies like "Agent Cody Banks," "Walk Hard: The Dewey Cox Story" and "The Black String." He is a father to 5-year-old son Mauz with Paige Muniz , who he married in 2019. On July 1, they revealed that they had been separated for an unspecified period of time and were now divorcing. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Could Still Reunite With Tyreek Hill Despite Chiefs’ Josh Downs Trade
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs have made another move to strengthen Patrick Mahomes’ receiving corps ahead of the rest of the 2026 season. Acquiring Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts has not ruled out a reunion with former Chiefs receiver Tyreek Hill. Chiefs keep Tyreek Hill option open after Downs trade According to a report, the Kansas City Chiefs remain interested in Tyreek Hill even after acquiring Josh Downs from Indianapolis. Hill remains under consideration as he continues recovering from a knee injury. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, recently offered an update on his expected return during the 2026 NFL season. Jan 5, 2025; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill (10) on the field before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Kansas City acquired Downs before the November 10 trade deadline, sending Indianapolis its 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks. The Chiefs received Downs and a 2027 seventh-round selection. Before the trade, Downs recorded 33 receptions for 354 yards and one touchdown in nine games. Primarily a slot receiver, he gives Patrick Mahomes another option in the passing game. The move addressed depth concerns in Kansas City’s receiving corps. Tyquan Thornton suffered a season-ending injury, while Rashee Rice also dealt with a hamstring issue. Downs’ arrival adds depth to the offense while leaving future roster decisions open. Kansas City’s interest in Hill reportedly dates back to October, when the team contacted his agent, Rosenhaus, about a possible reunion. Hill played alongside Mahomes from 2016 through 2021 and helped the Chiefs win Super Bowl LIV. However, no agreement has been reached regarding his return. Hill dislocated his knee during a September 29, 2025, game against the New York Jets, suffering damage to multiple ligaments, including his ACL. He underwent surgery and missed the remainder of the season. In July 2026, Hill said he was still working to regain strength in his left leg during rehabilitation. On November 10, Rosenhaus discussed Hill’s recovery during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. He said the receiver was close to receiving medical clearance and expected him to return during the 2026 season. “I’ll be working the phones for our guys that wanna be traded,” Rosenhaus said . “Right now I’m still working the phones for Tyreek Hill,” he added. His legal situation presents another potential obstacle. The NFL is investigating Hill under its Personal Conduct Policy following a civil case involving his estranged wife. A jury found him liable on two battery claims and ordered him to pay $500,000 in damages. The league has not announced a final disciplinary decision, leaving the possibility of suspension unresolved. The Kansas City Chiefs have strengthened their receiving group with the addition of Downs while continuing to monitor Hill’s recovery and the league’s review process. item.title: Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski joins Randy Johnson, Justin Verlander in exclusive Cy Young, World Series club
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski joins Randy Johnson, Justin Verlander in exclusive Cy Young, World Series club appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jacob Misiorowski is the National League’s Cy Young Award winner after the Milwaukee Brewers ace was finally announced as the 2026 winner on Wednesday. Coming off a sensational second season in the big leagues, Misiorowski got another reason to celebrate in the offseason. In addition to the World Series title he won with the Brewers by beating the Tampa Bay Rays in this year’s edition of the Fall Classic, the hard-throwing Misiorowski is now the fourth Brewer in franchise history to win the Cy Young. But there’s more . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Because Jacob Misiorowski won a World Series and a Cy Young Award in the same year, he also joined an extremely exclusive group of pitchers in MLB history. “The Miz has won the NL Cy Young. Jacob Misiorowski joins Randy Johnson and Justin Verlander as the only pitchers since 2000 to win both the Cy Young and the World Series in the same season,” SportsCenter shared via a social media post on X (formerly Twitter). Misiorowski put on a masterclass on nearly every night he pitched in 2026. Through 30 starts, he went 16-5. His ERA (1.80), total strikeouts (252) and WHIP (0.802) were all the best not just in the National League but in both leagues. Still just 24 years old, Misiorowski has so much in front of him, even though he’s already accomplished what countless others never achieved in their entire baseball careers. As long as he’s healthy, Misiorowski should be an intimidating pitcher to deal with opposing batters in years to come, including in 2027, when the Brewers look to defend their crown. Related: Brewers star Jacob Misiorowski’s ‘awesome’ admission after winning Cy Young following World Series Related: Jacob Misiorowski becomes fourth Brewers pitcher ever to win Cy Young Award

item.title: Devin Booker and the Suns are committed to working together for the rest of his career
item.description: Devin Booker and the Suns are committed to working together for the rest of his career originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ever since the Phoenix Suns selected Devin Booker 13th overall in the 2015 NBA Draft, they have been committed to bringing winning basketball to the city. The results have been mixed, but it has been clear that Booker deserves to be the star. He has been the Suns ' best player over the past decade, cementing his place as one of the franchise's all-time greats. They were only two wins away from a championship in 2021, but the Milwaukee Bucks got away with the victory. Devin Booker is focused on staying as the Suns' star player In the 2026-27 NBA season, the Suns are still a middle-of-the-road team. However, Booker has remained productive for the Suns. He has lived up to his role as the team's superstar, averaging 25.1 points and 4.8 assists per game this season. Unfortunately, it seems that the Suns are far away from a championship. They want to win a title, but the Suns might n not have the contender-worthy roster that they had in the early 2020s when Booker had the likes of Mikal Bridges, Deandre Ayton, and Chris Paul with him. MORE: Devin Booker is firm in his chase for a championship with the Suns This has led to discourse regarding Booker potentially asking out and looking for a challenge elsewhere. Despite that, it seems that Booker and the Suns are together in their quest to win a title. "From every indication that I've got, the Phoenix Suns want to keep Devin Booker, and they want to continue to build around him. For Devin Booker, he wants to be a Sun for life, ideally... It's about trying to make the team better around him," Michael Scotto said about Booker's place on the team while on SiriusXM NBA Radio . It is definitely a tough situation for Booker and the Suns. However, they are committed to each other, as they want to keep competing and prove that they can be competitive against any team. item.title: Paraguay partially refunds Ueno Bank depositors after collapse
item.description: Paraguay's Central Bank said Wednesday it had partially returned savings to all eligible Ueno Bank depositors, following the lender's collapse last week. The crisis triggered mass protests and the impeachment and arrest of former president Santiago Pena, who is accused of directing government funds to the bank.

item.title: Russian cloud Yandex says drone attacks on its datacenters caused data loss
item.description: Russian cloud operator Yandex has admitted to data loss after a drone attack on one of its datacenters. The attack, which Ukrainian press said was ordered by Kyiv, happened in early October and caused a fire and subsequent outage at Yandex’s ru-central1-b availability zone. Subsequent strikes targeted more Yandex datacenters and disrupted more of the company’s cloud and payment services. On Tuesday, Yandex posted an update on its recovery efforts, which it spun as something of a triumph because it restored over 97 percent of customer data. Of course that also means the company lost 2.84 percent of customer data, which it blamed on “critical hardware damage and a lack of backups on the platform.” It’s unclear if Yandex’s use of the phrase “on the platform” indicates it doesn’t keep backups of its own cloud, if whatever resilience techniques it employs don’t create multiple copies of customer data, or if clients didn’t protect their data. Whatever happened, Yandex has decided to enable backups by default for all VMs customers create in its cloud. That decision will mean customers will consume and pay for more Yandex resources, unless they opt out of the automated backups. Given that drones damaged three Yandex locations, and the war with Ukraine continues, users have good reasons to consider alternatives to its services. Indeed, Yandex’s announcement of its recovery efforts links to a page extolling the virtues of a hybrid cloud when devising data protection strategies. That page also mentions Yandex’s own Stackland product, which brings its stack on-prem, as an example of a hybrid approach. On Wednesday the company also launched a new availability zone named ru-central1-f. Yandex didn’t say where it’s located, other than to say it’s in “a new location.” Interestingly, Yandex has imposed quotas that limit the amount of resources users can access in the new availability zone and says it can’t yet handle traffic to private endpoints at the new facility. Many nations have imposed sanctions that restrict sales of technology products to Russia. It’s therefore unsurprising that Yandex might struggle to provision enough infrastructure to allow untrammeled access to a new availability zone. ®

item.title: Gowon’s memoirs: Nigeria owes Awolowo an eternal debt, by Olu Fasan
item.description: Last week, I started a discussion of General Yakubu Gowon’s multi-themed memoirs, My Life of Duty & Allegiance. My focus was on the book’s general tone, which I find unduly self-justificatory. In his attempts to defend his legacy, General Gowon presents himself as a saintly figure who did no wrong as a leader, whereas some introspection and nuanced reflection would have helped. That said, the book is a treasure trove of insightful details that enrich our historical narrative. This week, I will focus on one of such insights, namely, the quality of governance and public service ethos under General Gowon’s regime, with Chief Obafemi Awolowo singled out as the arrowhead of a remarkable governance approach that, if replicated today, would transform how Nigeria is governed and, thus, this country’s fortunes. As a political economist and policy practitioner who spent nearly 20 years advising the UK government on diverse policy areas, in addition to teaching public policy, I have professional and intellectual interests in how government is run. Thus, I was enthralled by General Gowon’s fascinating accounts of how the affairs of state were conducted under his administration, with the triumvirate of politicians (as ministers), civil servants (as technocrats), and universities and think-tanks (as sounding boards) driving policy formulation and implementation and setting standards of good and effective governance. Sitting atop the triumvirate was Chief Awolowo, an extraordinarily transformative leader! Indeed, if General Gowon’s memoirs can be said to have a hero, that hero is Chief Obafemi Awolowo, appointed by Gowon as the Vice Chairman of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, and Commissioner of Finance in his administration. In every reference to Chief Awolowo in the memoirs, General Gowon writes glowingly and superlatively about him. Gowon also gives credit to his colleagues in the Supreme Military Council, SMC, and the first-class mandarins who ran the civil service for his administration’s successes, especially its ability to prosecute a 30-month civil war “without endangering the national economy”. But he reserves his most generous praise for Chief Awolowo. Hear Gowon: “Chief Awolowo’s business acumen, political sagacity, economic wizardry and thorough man-management ability would later prove quite useful and helpful in ensuring that we kept our finances intact during and immediately after the civil war that broke out a few weeks after his appointment to the FEC.” He adds: “Without any argument, he made invaluable contributions.” Of course, Chief Awolowo’s reputation preceded him. As the premier of the Western Region, he performed so superbly that Harold Wilson, then British prime minister, described him as a “world-class leader”, who would make an outstanding President of America or Prime Minister of Britain.
